{{Quote|I'm a walking nerve cluster.|Durge|<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: The New Face of War">''[[Star Wars: Republic: The New Face of War]]''</ref>}}
The '''Gen'Dai''' were a seemingly immortal, formless [[Species/Legends|species]] which originated on an [[Gen'Dai homeworld/Legends|unidentified]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Devoid of any [[Skeleton/Legends|bones]], the Gen'Dai typically wore heavy [[Armor/Legends|armor]] to give themselves a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] structure.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:GenDai_TCWCG.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A Gen'Dai without an armor.]]
A boneless species (with large fangs), the Gen'Dai were virtually a formless jumble of corded muscle and nerve bundles. Because of this, Gen'Dai typically inhabited heavy armor made for [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] to give themselves a form which passed for any number of [[Species/Legends|species]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The only distinct feature of the Gen'Dai were their heads; typically bald, the Gen'Dai faces were humanoid with two eyes, a nose, and a mouth full of razor-sharp teeth. Two large, wing-like ears protruded from the sides of their heads; Gen'Dai typically tucked their ears under their jaw-line when wearing helmets to hide any distinguishing features. Lacking the vulnerable vital organs of most species, including [[Heart/Legends|hearts]] and [[Lung/Legends|lungs]], Gen'Dai could take extreme injuries and even complete [[Dismemberment/Legends|dismemberment]], and survive which gave them the reputation of being immortal. In fact, they could regrow lost limbs or other body parts in only a few minutes.<ref name="TCWCG" /> Unlike most species, Gen'Dai had a nervous system which was distributed throughout the body in the form of millions of nerve clusters. This fact gave the species near instantaneous reflexes as well as the ability to sustain a high volume of injuries without any overall damage. So high was their sensory acuity, that the Gen'Dai were able to feel a [[Human/Legends|Human's]] heartbeat from ranges of up to 200 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="TCWCG" />

[[File:GeD.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The bounty hunter Durge with most of his armor blown away by a missile.]]
As the Gen'Dai did not possess a heart, their circulatory system functioned by way of a series of capillaries and muscular contractions which pushed blood through the body. If the Gen'Dai received a cut, that area could easily be cut off from heavy blood-flow to prevent bleeding to death while the body regenerated itself. One of the Gen'Dai's few weaknesses was that they could be forced into an extended period of [[Hibernation trance/Legends|hibernation]] if they took too many severe injuries across their entire form. During this time the Gen'Dai's regenerative abilities replaced the body mass which was lost. Ultimately there were only two ways a Gen'Dai could be permanently killed. The first was the complete vaporization or incineration of one's body; such was case with Durge when he was sent into a star. The second was the death of a Gen'Dai's [[Brain/Legends|brain]] via physical destruction, as it was the only aspect of their bodies that could not be regenerated fully. Notably, the brain also degenerated over time like most species, which caused a form of [[psychosis]] to develop in Gen'Dai of advanced age.<ref name="TCWCG" />

==History==
The peaceful [[Gen'Dai homeworld/Legends|Gen'Dai homeworld]] was discovered sometime after the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] by the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. The Gen'Dai species was decimated in the ensuing battle, with an unknown number escaping the planet before it was lost to history.<ref name="The Flame" /> Leaving their world behind, the remaining Gen'Dai were scattered to the stars, seeking out a nomadic existence from [[Planet/Legends|planet]] to planet.<ref name="TCWCG" />

Over the course of galactic history, the Gen'Dai were largely absent from many of the great wars which plagued the established central government, only appearing time to time as the leaders of crime syndicates or [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]. These individuals typically suffered from psychosis stemming from the degeneration of brain tissue due to advanced age.<ref name="TCWCG" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Earlydurge.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Durge wearing traditional armor without a face mask.]]
A peaceful species, the Gen'Dai practiced a philosophy of "perfection of permanence", a belief that all change is an illusion. Because of this, the Gen'Dai philosophers preached that taking an active role in anything was pointless and detrimental. Having no official government or organization structure following the destruction of their homeworld, the Gen'Dai embraced the spirit of nomadic living and journeyed the stars largely in isolation. As their lifespans were so long, ranging from 4,000 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] to over 7,000, Gen'Dai rarely reproduced and had an exceptionally low birth rate.<ref name="TCWCG" />

While the population as a whole was made up of philosophers, the older population suffered from mental deterioration which led to a pronounced increase in violent tendencies. These rogues tended to take jobs as [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], poorly representing the species as cruel, heartless savages.<ref name="TCWCG" />

==Gen'Dai in the galaxy==
[[File:DurgeFace-Obsession3.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Durge after his face was badly burned by several violent explosions.]]
Rarely seen in the galaxy due to their low numbers, those few Gen'Dai encountered generally masked themselves in full armor to not only give them form, but also to blend in as a nondescript humanoid. Those who knew about the species thought of them as long-lived and hard to kill, and also wrongly associated them with vicious killers. This erroneous generalization stemmed from the fact that the most famous Gen'Dai in the galaxy had succumbed to an age-related psychosis which brought out violent tendencies.<ref name="TCWCG" />

Active during the events of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], two other Gen'Dai were recorded by the galactic history: the leader of the [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] anti-Imperial resistance [[the Flame]]<ref name="The Flame" /> and the [[Locust]] on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]]. A band of Gen'Dai known as [[Bala D'ur]] had a [[Bala D'ur Hideout|hideout]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]],<ref name="Humanitarian Aid">{{TORcite|type=heroic|Humanitarian Aid|[[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]}}</ref> and several Gen'Dai referred to as "Immortal Guardians" were an elite security force on payroll of [[Karagga]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]].<ref name="Karagga">{{TORcite|type=operation|Karagga's Palace}}</ref> During the [[Conquest of Makeb|Conquest]] of [[Makeb]] after Karagga's death, a [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Cartel]] Gen'Dai Warlord named [[Sunder (mercenary)|Sunder]] raised an army with other Cartel Warlords on [[Darvannis]].<ref name="Darvannis">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=operation|Scum and Villainy}}</ref>

Arguably history's best known Gen'Dai was the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Commander/Legends|commander]], [[Durge/Legends|Durge]]. Active during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Confederacy and the Republic, Durge was completely insane by the time of the war and possessed an unequivocal blood lust. Durge was responsible for the [[Battle of Ohma-D'un|slaughter]] of [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] colonists on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]] and the deaths of several [[Jedi/Legends|members]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], such as [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Glaive (Jedi)|Glaive]]<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: The New Face of War" /> and [[Jon Antilles]].<ref name="Republic 53">[[Republic 53|''Republic'' 53]]</ref>
